newsitem.title: CANADA: Dominion Bond says Canada banks in transition.
newsitem.headline: Dominion Bond says Canada banks in transition.

text.p: Dominion Bond Rating Service said on Wednesday that Canada's six major banks were undergoing a major transition because of demographic changes to the retail and commercial sectors.
The Toronto-based ratings agency identified three areas of significant change in its report entitled "Dis-intermediation in Canadian Banking".

DBRS said that for the first time in years growth in retail deposits was insufficient to finance the growth in retail loans as baby boomers shrank their savings accounts in favor of higher return investments in mutual funds and stocks.

The rating agency said the shrinking retail deposits meant that the banks would be required to raise more costly wholesale funds from large cash pools such as pension plans and investment funds, which would demand a higher premium than what was paid on retail savings accounts.

The report said corporations were also finding alternatives to bank financing through share offerings and debt issues, leading the banks and trust companies to reduce their risk to such weighted assets to improve capital ratios, liquidity and off balance sheet efficiency.
The report noted that direct capital markets financing was becoming the main source of more flexible lower cost funding for Canadian corporations.
Canada's commercial paper market increased to C$48 billion in 1996 from C$41 billion the previous year.

Dominion said the changes would not materially affect the creditworthiness of the big six banks, but the increasing dependence on the financial markets could mean a slower pace of growth if market activity declined.

"The Canadian banking sector has continued to perform well, with another year of strong growth in fiscal 1996. While earnings are expected to continue to improve in 1997, the pace of growth will likely slow, depending upon conditions in the financial markets," Dominion said in a statement about its report.
"As with other global banking groups rated by DBRS, performance by the Canadian banks is becoming more market driven."
